text: canvasquiz package provides functions interact Canvas LMS API, specifically constructing quizzes retrieving quiz data. package allows write quizzes R directly push Canvas, well retrieve quiz statistics results analysis. Note package supports Classic Quizzes Canvas, New Quizzes.

code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("emitanaka/canvasquiz")

title: Quiz For Canvas Learning Management System
code: library(canvasquiz)

title: Quiz For Canvas Learning Management System
text: R environment, can set following environment variables avoid specify function call: set .Renviron file persistence across sessions. can use usethis package edit .Renviron file: URL base URL Canvas instance, e.g. ANU https://canvas.anu.edu.au. access token can generated Canvas account settings “Approved Integrations”. course ID can found URL course Canvas. example course URL https://canvas.anu.edu.au/courses/12345, course ID 12345.
code: Sys.setenv(CANVASQUIZ_COURSE_ID = "your_course_id") Sys.setenv(CANVASQUIZ_URL = "https://your_canvas_instance.instructure.com") Sys.setenv(CANVASQUIZ_TOKEN = "your_access_token") usethis::edit_r_environ()

title: Quiz For Canvas Learning Management System
text: output quiz ID newly created quiz. Use quiz ID add questions quiz. quiz ID specified, question added recently created quiz.
code: qid <- create_quiz(title = "Quiz 1",                     description = "This assessment is 30 minutes with only one attempt.",                    quiz_type = "practice_quiz",                    attempts = attempt_options(n = 1, time = 30))

title: Quiz For Canvas Learning Management System
text: exact value match: value match tolerance: value match specified number decimal places: value match within specified range:
code: create_question("What is 2 + 2?",                 answers = answer_num(4),                 points = 1,                 quiz_id = qid) create_question("What is the square root of 2?",                 answers = answer_num(sqrt(2), tol = 0.1),                 points = 1,                 quiz_id = qid) create_question("What is the square root of 2?",                 answers = answer_num_precision(sqrt(2), precision = 1),                 points = 1,                 quiz_id = qid) create_question("What is the value of pi?",                 answers = answer_num_range(3.14, 3.15),                 points = 1,                 quiz_id = qid)

text: multiple choice question one correct answer: multiple choice question multiple correct answers:

code: create_question("Match the following countries with their capitals.",                 answers = answer_matching(                   left = c("France", "Japan", "Australia"),                   right = c("Paris", "Tokyo", "Canberra"),                   extra_choices = c("Madrid", "Beijing", "Wellington")                 ),                 quiz_id = qid)

title: Create an answer object for a quiz question — answer_single
text: function wrapper creates appropriate answer object based input. can handle multiple choice questions, true/false questions, short answer questions, numerical questions (exact answers, precision-based answers, range-based answers), matching questions. function automatically determine type question based format input create corresponding answer object using appropriate helper functions.

title: Create an answer object for a quiz question — answer_single
text: x correct answer(s) question. See details expected format based type question. y Additional parameter certain question types. See details expected format based type question. tol acceptable error margin answer. Defaults 0 exact answer. precision number decimal places answer must correct .

title: Create an answer object for a quiz question — answer_single
text: function uses following logic determine type question: x logical value y NULL, creates true/false question using answer_true_false(). x single numeric value y NULL, creates numerical question exact answer using answer_num(). tol greater 0, creates numerical question error margin. precision greater 0, creates numerical question specified precision. x numeric vector length 2, creates numerical question range-based answer using answer_num_range(). Alternatively, x single numeric value y single numeric value, also creates numerical question range-based answer using answer_num_range(), x lower bound y upper bound. x named character vector, creates matching question using answer_matching(). extra choices matching question can provided y. x y character vectors, creates multiple choice question using answer_mcq(). input format match cases, function throws error indicating answer format unsupported.
